title: Falcon Concept Map
subtitle: From Falcon at the center out to modules, then features. Tap a bubble.
rootDesc: A cloud-native security platform running on a single, lightweight agent (sensor). Analysis and correlation happen not on the endpoint, but in CrowdStrike's cloud (Threat Graph).

modules.title: Falcon Insight
modules.desc: The core of the platform. Continuously monitors process, file, network, and registry events on endpoints; performs behavior-based (IOA) threat detection.

children.title: Detections
children.desc: The alert list. Comes with a severity rating (critical/high/medium/low) and a MITRE ATT&CK tactic/technique mapping.

children.title: Process Tree
children.desc: Visually shows which parent-child process chain triggered a detection.

children.title: Host Timeline
children.desc: A chronological record of every event that happened on a host over time.

children.title: IOA vs IOC
children.desc: IOA = behavioral signal. IOC = static artifact (hash, IP, filename). Falcon relies primarily on IOAs.

children.title: Falcon Score
children.desc: Automatic risk scoring — which alert to look at first.

modules.title: Falcon Prevent
modules.desc: Next-gen antivirus. Blocks known and unknown malware using machine learning and behavioral rules instead of signatures.

children.title: ML-based static analysis
children.desc: Predicts whether a file is malicious using an ML model before it even runs.

children.title: Behavioral blocking
children.desc: A running process is stopped the moment it shows a malicious behavior pattern.

children.title: Quarantine
children.desc: A suspicious/malicious file is isolated and cleaned without impacting the system.

modules.title: Falcon OverWatch
modules.desc: CrowdStrike's own 24/7 proactive threat hunting service, staffed by human analysts — catches subtle signals that automation misses.

children.title: Proactive hunting
children.desc: Actively hunts for threats hiding in the environment, without waiting for an alert.

children.title: Escalation
children.desc: Reports a suspicious finding directly to your own SOC team.

modules.title: Falcon Complete
modules.desc: CrowdStrike handles monitoring and response on your behalf, with SLA guarantees.

children.title: SLA-backed response
children.desc: A guaranteed time commitment from detection through to remediation.

modules.title: Falcon Spotlight
modules.desc: Detects known vulnerabilities (CVEs) on a system using the same Falcon sensor, with no separate scanning agent needed.

children.title: Exploitability prioritization
children.desc: Ranks vulnerabilities by how genuinely likely they are to be exploited.

modules.title: Falcon Identity Protection
modules.desc: Detects AD and identity-based attacks — catches abnormal authentication behavior via LDAP traffic and credential usage patterns.

children.title: Lateral movement detection
children.desc: Catches the pattern of a stolen credential being used across different machines.

children.title: AD integration
children.desc: Monitors authentication traffic on Domain Controllers in real time.

modules.title: Falcon X
modules.desc: Enriches a detected file/hash/IP with CrowdStrike's global threat intelligence.

children.title: Hash / IOC enrichment
children.desc: Places a local detection into global context — where this IOC has been seen before, by whom.

modules.title: Falcon Next-Gen SIEM
modules.desc: A SIEM layer that ingests third-party log sources (firewall, Exchange, IronPort, etc.) and analyzes them with correlation rules.

children.title: 3rd-party data onboarding
children.desc: Logs from systems outside Falcon can also be piped in here.

children.title: Fusion SOAR
children.desc: Runs an automated action (playbook) after a detection fires.

modules.title: MITRE in Falcon
modules.desc: Falcon labels every detection with where it sits in an attack, using MITRE ATT&CK as the backbone. Verify the exact category names against the 'MITRE-Based Falcon Detections Framework' page in the CrowdStrike docs.

children.title: Tactic & technique label
children.desc: Each detection shows an ATT&CK tactic and technique, often with the ID (for example Credential Access via OS Credential Dumping, T1003). The label explains why the behavior is considered malicious.

children.title: Objective layer
children.desc: Above tactics, CrowdStrike groups detections by the attacker's broader objective — such as gaining access, keeping access, or following through — so an analyst sees how far the attack has progressed.

children.title: Non-ATT&CK categories
children.desc: Detections that come from a method rather than a behavior — machine learning on a file, known malware, intel or custom IOC matches — appear under CrowdStrike's own tactic names instead of an ATT&CK tactic.

children.title: Why the mapping helps
children.desc: The analyst immediately knows the stage: Execution means something ran; Credential Access or Lateral Movement means the attack is already spreading and urgency rises.

children.title: Linking out
children.desc: The technique ID connects the detection to the ATT&CK page: other ways the same goal is reached, mitigations, and groups known to use it.

children.title: Coverage
children.desc: Because detections are mapped, detection coverage can be laid over the ATT&CK matrix to see which techniques are and are not covered.

modules.title: Detection Anatomy
modules.desc: The fields an analyst reads in a Falcon detection, and what each one answers. Most appear both in the detection summary and on the process node that triggered it.

children.title: Host
children.desc: Hostname, OS, sensor (agent) ID, last-seen IP, site or OU, and host groups — which machine, and what kind.

children.title: User
children.desc: The account the process ran as, and the logon session. Tells you whether a person, a service account, or SYSTEM was involved.

children.title: Process & command line
children.desc: File name, full path, and the exact command line with arguments. Usually the single most revealing field: encoded PowerShell or a download URL shows intent.

children.title: Hashes
children.desc: SHA-256 and MD5 of the file, used for reputation lookups and to search whether the same file ran on other hosts.

children.title: Network & DNS
children.desc: Connections the process made and domains it resolved — candidate C2 servers and download sources.

children.title: Verdict & action
children.desc: Severity, the tactic and technique, a description of the behavior, and what Falcon already did: blocked, killed the process, quarantined the file, or only detected.

modules.title: Reading a Process Tree
modules.desc: The chain of processes that led to the detection, from the earliest ancestor down to what the triggering process spawned. Context that a single event cannot give.

children.title: Parent-child
children.desc: Every process is started by another. explorer.exe → winword.exe is a user opening a document; winword.exe → powershell.exe is a document running code.

children.title: Triggering process
children.desc: The node that matched the detection logic is highlighted. Read upward for how it started, downward for what it did next.

children.title: Suspicious lineages
children.desc: Office or browser spawning a shell, a service host launching a script from a temp folder, rundll32 with no arguments, a process named like a system file in the wrong path.

children.title: Per-node details
children.desc: Each node carries its own command line, user, hashes, and network and file activity, so the whole story can be read from the tree.

children.title: Scope
children.desc: Siblings and children show whether the attack went further — a dropped file, a scheduled task, a connection out.

modules.title: Analyst Workflow
modules.desc: One reasonable order for working a detection, from first look to closing it.

children.title: 1. Read the summary
children.desc: Severity, tactic and technique, and what action Falcon already took. A blocked execution is less urgent than a detection-only credential dump.

children.title: 2. Context
children.desc: Which host and user: server or workstation, admin or regular user, critical asset or test machine.

children.title: 3. Process tree & command line
children.desc: Reconstruct what happened and whether it makes sense — an IT script, an installer, or an attack.

children.title: 4. Enrich
children.desc: Look up hashes, domains, and IPs in threat intel and reputation services.

children.title: 5. Scope
children.desc: Search for the same hash, command line, or domain on other hosts. One host or many?

children.title: 6. Decide and act
children.desc: True positive: contain (network-isolate the host, kill, quarantine) and escalate. False positive: close with a clear reason, and suggest tuning so it does not recur.
